steps.title: Plan a robust Hi-Lo update
steps.objective: Apply the chapter's testing, contract, and failure-policy ideas before coding.
steps.explanation:
Use these checkpoints for the game:

- **Verify behavior:** unit tests isolate functions; frameworks organize checks; integration tests exercise connections. Compilation is not verification. Adding unrelated features is scope creep.
- **Measure execution:** statement coverage is exercised statements / total statements; branch coverage is exercised outcomes / total outcomes. Both are percentages, not correctness proofs. Test loops for 0, 1, and 2 iterations.
- **Handle failures:** the happy path has no errors; sad paths do. Robust code retries recoverable bad input, stops or propagates fatal failures that prevent continuation, and uses std::cerr for diagnostics. EOF ends this game normally.
- **State contracts:** preconditions hold before work, invariants remain true during it, and postconditions hold afterward. Input retries must preserve the next valid attempt number.
- **Check bugs:** runtime assert (<cassert>) terminates on a false condition when enabled; NDEBUG commonly disables it in release builds. Keep required work outside assertions. static_assert rejects false constant expressions at compile time, regardless of NDEBUG. Assert impossible internal states; handle possible user errors normally.

[Source: LearnCpp 9.x](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-9-summary-and-quiz/), Alex, updated December 1, 2024; fetched October 19, 2026. Its single Quiz #1 is adapted in the next two coding stages, retaining [8.x Quiz #3](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-8-summary-and-quiz/).

questions.question: Readers pass isolated tests, but replay consumes leftover guess text. Which next action fits this input-repair phase?
options: Run a guessing-through-replay integration case; keep the reader unit checks.
questions.explanation: Exercise the connection where the failure occurs. A framework can retain these checks; unrelated features would expand scope.

questions.question: A suite reaches 8 of 10 statements and 3 of 4 branch outcomes. What evidence does it provide?
options: 80% statement and 75% branch coverage; still add relevant expectations and 0/1/2 loop cases.
80% proof of correctness; loop checks are redundant.
questions.explanation: Coverage measures execution. It does not establish correct results, input boundaries, or loop behavior.

questions.question: Which contract matches Hi-Lo input recovery?
options: Precondition: the player wins; invariant: every line spends a guess; postcondition: input never ends.
Precondition: positive bounds contain the target; invariant: retries preserve the next valid attempt number; winning postcondition: an accepted guess equals the target.
Precondition: all user input is valid; invariant: count is always zero; postcondition: EOF means a loss.
questions.explanation: The caller controls the target contract; the reader handles user mistakes without spending attempts; a win requires equality.

questions.question: Which implementation handles a mistyped guess without making release behavior depend on assertions?
options: Read and validate only inside assert(getGuess(...) > 0).
Use static_assert to inspect the current input stream.
Read and recover normally; reserve assert for internal bugs and static_assert for constant configuration checks.
questions.explanation: Mistypes are possible sad paths, not impossible states. NDEBUG removes assert's expression, including side effects; static_assert cannot inspect runtime input.

steps.title: Repair both Hi-Lo input boundaries
steps.objective: Implement the source quiz's guess reader and replay reader without leaving trailing input behind.
steps.explanation:
[LearnCpp 9.x Quiz #1](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-9-summary-and-quiz/) upgrades Hi-Lo for invalid guesses and trailing characters at guess/replay prompts. Separate guess reading from gameplay. A buffer temporarily holds input; token extraction leaves the rest of its line waiting.

- **getGuess(count, low, high):** prompt Guess #N: before each read; extract an int and discard the rest of the line. Retry malformed, overflowing, or out-of-range values without changing count. Return an in-range value. Follow the source solution: 43x accepts 43 and discards x.
- **playAgain():** prompt Replay (y/n):, read the first non-whitespace character, and discard its line. Accept lowercase y/n; retry other responses. Thus yes accepts y and no thanks accepts n.
- **Browser termination policy:** getGuess returns -1 on EOF, badbit, or invalid bounds (low must be positive and no greater than high); playAgain returns false on EOF/badbit. A successfully extracted final token without a newline still counts. Never retry terminal failure forever.

The supplied main demonstrates the readers; the next stage integrates the game.

hints: Remember whether extraction succeeded before you clear failbit. Do not treat eofbit after a successful final extraction as an invalid value.
On recoverable extraction failure, clear the failure before ignore(max, '\n'); otherwise ignore cannot discard the bad line.
Discard the rest of every attempted line, even a valid numeric prefix or an accepted replay response.
Return on EOF or badbit instead of repeating a read that cannot succeed.
examples: Input x, 0, 101, then 43x on separate lines: getGuess(1, 1, 100) returns 43 after four prompts, all numbered 1.
Input q, yes, no thanks on separate lines: successive playAgain() calls return true, then false.
Final input 100 without a newline is valid; a later read returns -1.

steps.title: Put recovery into the complete game
steps.objective: Finish Hi-Lo while ensuring that only valid guesses spend attempts and replay begins with clean input.
steps.explanation:
Finish [LearnCpp 9.x Quiz #1](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-9-summary-and-quiz/), retaining the game from [8.x Quiz #3](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-8-summary-and-quiz/). Keep the supplied readers.

**playHiLo(number, guesses, low, high)**
- Announce Round: L..H; tries G. Read valid attempts numbered 1 through guesses; retries spend no attempts.
- Print Too high or Too low for wrong guesses. On equality print You win and return 1. After all attempts fail, print You lose; target N and return 0.
- Return -1 immediately on exhausted input, without a loss message. Each message ends with a newline. Caller preconditions: positive interval containing the target, positive attempt limit.

**runSession(nextTarget)**
- Request nextTarget(1, 100) exactly once per round; pass its result to playHiLo with seven attempts and bounds 1..100.
- After completed rounds, call playAgain and repeat on y. Stop immediately on an interrupted round. Print Thanks for playing and return 0, including at EOF.

**Supplied plumbing:** TargetSupplier is a function pointer taking two int bounds and returning an int target; call it like nextTarget(low, high). randomTarget uses the standard library for uniform random targets; main passes sessionTarget, initially randomTarget, into runSession. Preserve this wiring and RNG adapter. Tests substitute a deterministic supplier to check each request and target use, never expected random draws. Fresh draws may equal previous draws.

The supplier seam, replacement for external Random.h, short output labels, and EOF policy are browser adaptations.
steps.sourceExercise: adapted — Quiz Question #1 complete Hi-Lo update, retaining 8.x Quiz #3 game rules; self-contained random setup, supplied function-pointer target supplier and main wiring for deterministic multi-round tests, short output labels, and EOF result are browser adaptations

hints: Only the outer count loop spends attempts. getGuess retries internally using the same count.
Test the -1 sentinel before comparing a guess with the target; equality returns immediately.
The losing message belongs after the loop, not after every wrong guess.
Call nextTarget(1, 100) inside runSession's round loop, then pass its return value to playHiLo(number, 7, 1, 100). On an interrupted round, break before asking to replay.
examples: With target 42 and three attempts, lines x, 0, 101, 60extra, 20, 42suffix produce high, low, then a win; only three attempts are spent.
With target 100 and seven attempts, guesses 1 through 7 lose and reveal 100; an eighth line remains unread.
A completed round followed by y extra starts another random round. A later n extra ends the session.
A test supplier returning 100 then 1 must be called twice for two rounds. Each round can win on its seventh valid guess; real random targets need not differ.

steps.objective: Apply the chapter's validation and testing ideas to the repository's retained integration assignment.
steps.explanation:
Open the [existing notes](workspaces/09/09_x/lesson.md) and [learner main.cpp](workspaces/09/09_x/main.cpp). This extra repository task comes from lessons/09_x.json; it supplements the [LearnCpp Hi-Lo quiz](https://www.learncpp.com/cpp-tutorial/chapter-9-summary-and-quiz/) above.

- readBounded(low, high): follow the workspace's 9.5 line-reading policy, accept inclusive bounds, return -1 on EOF or reversed bounds. Check its notes/tests before transferring Hi-Lo's numeric-prefix policy.
- orderTotal(code, quantity): codes 1/2/3 cost 5/8/12; quantities are 1..20; invalid arguments return -1.
- placeOrder(): read product then quantity, return total or -1 on exhausted input. Quantity retries must not reread product. Print no prompts or totals.

Test units, then their connection: bad, 2, 0, 3 gives 24; 1 then EOF gives -1. Include endpoints, overflow, EOF at each stage, and final tokens without newlines. Retain supplied tests; add and explain one branch, boundary, or integration case. Run the workspace tests, then submit with ./course check 9.x from the repository root.
